case_a_same_qid_two_devices.note: the case the ruling names. A collision here would mean two devices share a multimodal cache entry.

case_b_same_qid_same_device_twice.note: a repeat by one device at a LATER opportunity. For single-shot the intended condition is cold per image, so these must also differ; that is the one place where SS deliberately forgoes the within-device reuse D84 otherwise preserves.

case_c_identical_image_content_different.note: the case a content-keyed cache WOULD hit and an identifier check would miss. StudySS1: by image id VizWiz val is 4,319 unique on 4,319 and passes clean, while 34 groups of byte-identical photos sat under different filenames.

negative_control.scheme: frame_ref alone, device and session dropped from the key
negative_control.note: collisions MUST appear here. They do not appear in the real scheme, so the real scheme is doing the work rather than the trace happening to hold no repeats.

n16.register: request bodies, not server behaviour. The server-side gate (mm_cache_queries > 0 AND mm_cache_hits == 0) is the H100's and is separate.
